title: Glass Jar

actions.label: Rinse & Empty Jar
actions.feedback: Jar rinsed and emptied. Eliminates sticky food and sauce residue that rots and fouls cullet washing plants.

actions.label: Remove Metal Lid
actions.feedback: Metal lid separated. Note: Rules differ by area—some facilities ask you to separate metal lids so they can be captured by overhead magnets, while other programs ask you to keep lids off.

outcomes.title: Glass Recycling Accepted
outcomes.text: Clean, empty glass jars are accepted in the Cyan Glass Recycling Bin and can be remelted infinitely without loss of quality.
outcomes.takeaway: Glass is 100% circular—recycling saves 30% furnace energy compared to virgin raw materials.

outcomes.title: Glass Stream Contaminated
outcomes.text: Unrinsed food remnants rot during transit and attract vermin at cullet processing yards.
outcomes.takeaway: Always rinse food containers before placing them in the recycling bin.

outcomes.title: Infinite Resource Landfilled
outcomes.text: Glass takes over 1 million years to decompose in a landfill, permanently locking away an infinitely recyclable resource.
outcomes.takeaway: Place clean glass in the designated Cyan Glass Recycling Bin or local drop-off center.

outcomes.title: Dangerous Hazard in Compost
outcomes.text: Glass does not decompose in organic compost and poses serious laceration hazards to compost processors and soil health.
outcomes.takeaway: Never place glass jars or bottles into organic compost bins.

guidanceNote: Consistent with app guidance: Place in Cyan Glass Recycling Bin; rinse clean. Lid action is informational and never penalized.
